robustness_summary.interpretation: The primary direction is stable across leave-one-out and decisive-only secondary analyses. Three-valid evidence is weaker and uncertainty spans zero; strict unanimity changes the estimand and has materially lower coverage.

dualswap_boundary.reason: DUAL_SWAP uses repeated canonical-pair-by-judge units without a frozen pair-level aggregation rule, while Multi-Judge uses one canonical-pair consensus decision.

scientific_rationale: The frozen primary matched comparison has a positive 4.87 percentage-point agreement difference with a 95% bootstrap CI entirely above zero on 1,125 retained pairs.
The result has transparent planned-pair coverage of 69.83% and explicit operational/split abstention accounting.
Leave-one-out analyses remain positive, decisive-only analysis remains positive, and all eight descriptive category deltas are positive.
Promotion is limited to a secondary RQ7 mitigation result; it neither replaces DUAL_SWAP nor supports a direct superiority claim.
approved_claims: Under the frozen strict four-judge consensus protocol, Multi-Judge Consensus increased agreement with human preference reference labels by 4.87 percentage points relative to the equal-weight individual-judge baseline on the same retained pairs (95% CI +4.02 to +5.73 pp), with 69.83% planned-pair coverage.

Multi-Judge Consensus is an official secondary mitigation strategy evaluating cross-judge aggregation; DUAL_SWAP remains the primary RQ7 mitigation result evaluating within-judge presentation-consistency filtering.
prohibited_claims: Bias is eliminated or causally mitigated.
The +4.87 pp Multi-Judge and +0.70 pp DUAL_SWAP deltas are directly comparable effects.
limitations: Coverage is 69.83% of planned pairs; abstention is an explicit operating trade-off.
Three-valid sensitivity is weaker and its secondary CI spans zero.
Strict unanimity has no matched gain and only 37.00% planned-pair coverage.
No direct DUAL_SWAP-versus-Multi-Judge superiority analysis is scientifically defensible.
